approach: Find how far the temperature can move away from 25 °C, in either direction, before the thermal expansion of the scale's length produces an error larger than the stated 0.5 mm accuracy.

steps.text: Write the length error produced by a temperature change ΔT away from 25 °C.
Set this error equal to the allowed 0.5 mm over the metre length and solve for the allowed |ΔT|.
The scale can be used within 50 °C on either side of the temperature at which it was made.

common_mistakes.text: Using 2 × 10⁻⁵ instead of the given 10⁻⁵ for α gives an allowed change of only 25 °C, and applying it symmetrically but forgetting the 25 °C base gives 0°C to +50°C.
Using 2 × 10⁻⁵ instead of the given 10⁻⁵ for α gives an allowed change of only 25 °C, and extending it in only the warmer direction from 25 °C gives +25°C to +50°C.
